solutions.check: 26 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Sandi Toksvig all over local woman?

indicators.note: to be all over something is to surround it on every side, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: the comedian Sandi Toksvig was born in Denmark
a local is a pub, abbreviated PH for public house

explanation.surface: A satirical jibe that Sandi Toksvig is all over some woman from the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local woman' reads as one phrase, but 'local' is the pub and only 'woman' defines; the question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Daphne is a female first name, so it is an example of a woman.

clue.text: After CSE fiasco, gutless Tory secures like, Transport

indicators.note: a fiasco is a shambles, so the letters before it end up in disorder
without guts means the inside is taken out, leaving only the outer letters
to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is held inside another
after places the next chunk behind the one named first

blocks.note: CSE was an old British school exam, here rearranged
only the first and last letters remain
as means like, in the sense of similar to

explanation.surface: A rambling complaint, full of teenage 'like', about a Tory exam blunder and public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like buses and trains, but it means rapture. The CSE was a lower-level school exam in England before GCSEs.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport in its literary sense is overwhelming emotion, a synonym for bliss or rapture.

clue.text: Miliband's conclusion: "I'm comedian!" – plonker!

indicators.note: a conclusion is an end, so the last letter of the name is taken

blocks.note: the final letter of the name
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
a wit is a funny person

explanation.surface: Ed Miliband sums up by claiming to be a comedian, and is jeered as a plonker.
explanation.walkthrough: Plonker is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A plonker is British slang for an idiot, the same insult as a stupid person.

clue.text: No knight, Cameron, one rejected – give the villain time!

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the whole string is read from end to start

blocks.note: no plus sir, the title of a knight
David Cameron was Prime Minister
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A knight is snubbed and Cameron is rejected while someone demands the criminal be locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal covers all three pieces, read backwards together; to give someone time is to sentence them to prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving a criminal time means a jail sentence, which is to lock them up.

clue.text: Endure dyke right to the very end

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for an adjective, as in a last-ditch stand

blocks.note: to last is to endure
a dyke can be a ditch or channel

explanation.surface: An instruction to put up with a waterway all the way to its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is made at the final moment, holding out until everything else has failed.

clue.text: Rum shenanigans within Labour – utter chaos

indicators.note: shenanigans are mischief and trickery, so the letters are played about with
within puts one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged
toil is hard labour

explanation.surface: Odd goings-on inside the Labour Party add up to total disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the party but is plain hard work; 'Rum' is the fodder, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great disturbance and confusion, matching complete chaos.

clue.text: see 13ac.
(& 23ac.) Scum politician finally getting City backing conjures up a dark picture

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
backing means going backwards, so the city name is read from end to start

blocks.note: a film is a thin layer of scum on a surface
the last letter of the word
the city of Rio de Janeiro

explanation.surface: A scummy politician gains backing from the City of London, which evokes something sinister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' tempts as the London financial district, but it is Rio de Janeiro.
explanation.definitionFit: Film noir is a genre of bleak, shadowy crime movies, so it is a dark motion picture.

clue.text: Chuck admits, at first "Like fleshy boobs to explode"

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: to chuck is to throw
the opening letter of the word
a fleshy bosom wobbles

explanation.surface: Someone called Chuck confesses that large breasts are about to burst out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a man's name but is the verb. To throw a wobbly is British slang for a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw a wobbly is British slang for having a sudden temper tantrum, an outburst of rage.

clue.text: Ex-Labour minister, Peter, to get rid of London area

blocks.note: Peter Shore was a Labour cabinet minister in the 1960s and 70s
to ditch is to get rid of

explanation.surface: An old Labour minister called Peter is to be dumped by a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Shoreditch is a district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoreditch is a trendy district in the East End of London.

clue.text: see 25ac.
Runs with Coe – excited, having an erection – get back!

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
the name of Sebastian Coe, rearranged
being aroused is being up

explanation.surface: Seb Coe goes running, gets aroused, and someone yells to retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian Coe is a former Olympic runner who led the London 2012 Games.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup is to recover money or losses, which is to regain them.

clue.text: (& 7dn.) Salmond's political ambition is "perverted, in-depth conceitedness"

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper form, so the quoted letters are twisted around

blocks.note: all twenty letters, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses Alex Salmond's great political goal as twisted, thoroughgoing vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: Alex Salmond, as First Minister of Scotland, led the SNP's campaign to leave the United Kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Salmond's lifelong aim as SNP leader was for Scotland to break away from the UK as a separate nation.

clue.text: ANC lied about source of aviation hazard?

indicators.note: about suggests moving round, so the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: the African National Congress, taken as letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: The ANC is accused of lying about what causes danger to aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2010 ash from the Icelandic volcano Eyjafjallajökull grounded flights across Europe, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcanic eruption in this North Atlantic country sent out an ash cloud that halted air travel.

clue.text: Terrorist devices: Clegg's initial answer, right, is a dead loss

indicators.note: initial means the first letter of the name

blocks.note: the opening letter of the name
A is the standard abbreviation for answer
R is the abbreviation for right
a show that bombs is a total failure

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that Nick Clegg's first response on terror weapons was hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bombs' here is the verb for failing utterly, not the explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Car bombs are explosives hidden in vehicles, a weapon used by terrorists.

clue.text: The purpose of a super-injunction is sick-making

blocks.note: first meaning: silencing the press
second meaning: causing one to retch

explanation.surface: An opinion that celebrity super-injunctions are nauseating.
explanation.walkthrough: Super-injunctions were British court orders, used notably by celebrities around 2011, that banned even reporting the order's existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Gagging is both silencing someone, as such court orders do, and choking or retching from disgust.

clue.text: One embroiled in legal fiasco – love the old heretic

indicators.note: a fiasco is a mess, so the letters before it are scrambled
to be embroiled in something is to be caught up inside it

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
the five letters rearranged
love is nil, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in a courtroom disaster is condemned as a heretic of old.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo was tried by the Inquisition in 1633 and found suspect of heresy for backing a sun-centred cosmos.

clue.text: Idealistic union to bump off my employer!

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for union
to top someone is slang for killing them
Ian Hislop, editor of Private Eye, where this puzzle appears

explanation.surface: The setter dreams of a trade union that would murder the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter writes for Private Eye, whose editor is Ian Hislop, so 'my employer' is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian describes visionary schemes for a perfect society, so it means idealistic.

clue.text: Female leader of Tories welcoming Steptoe and Son a bit?

indicators.note: the leader is the front letter of the word that follows
to welcome someone is to take them in, so a piece goes inside

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
the father and son of the sitcom Steptoe and Son are rag-and-bone men, junk dealers
the front letter of the word

explanation.surface: A woman leading the Conservatives takes in a pair of TV junk dealers, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female leader of Tories' reads as one woman, but splits into a female and the first letter. Steptoe and Son was a British sitcom about rag-and-bone men.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment is a small piece broken off something, so it is a little portion.

clue.text: The Almighty working to guard rear of pisspoor Brown?

indicators.note: the rear is the back, so the last letter of the next word is taken
a guard surrounds what it protects, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: God is the Almighty
the last letter of the word
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A question whether God himself is now working to protect the dismal Prime Minister Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Gordon is one Brown, the former Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Gordon Brown was the UK Labour Prime Minister, so his first name identifies one Brown.

clue.text: Internet-connected person preceding this is cause of Tube delay?

blocks.note: the plain meaning: hooked up to the web

blocks.clueFragment: person preceding this is cause of Tube delay?
blocks.note: the setter's reading: put 'person' before the answer and you get the London Underground announcement for someone hit on the track

explanation.surface: A web user is blamed for holding up the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person under a train' is announced on the Tube as a 'person on the line', so 'person' plus this two-word phrase explains the delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being connected to the internet is the plain sense of the word, as opposed to offline.

clue.text: One who gives head aggressively

blocks.note: the surface reading: a crude sexual sense
the setter's reading: someone who headbutts people, which is British slang for nutting them

explanation.walkthrough: The vulgar sense of 'gives head' is a decoy; in British slang to nut someone is to headbutt them, and the word also means a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a nutter is a crazy or violent person, here taken literally as someone who delivers headbutts.

clue.text: see 8ac.
Nickname of Brown? Yes – and certainly no!

blocks.note: the plain sense: what Lancelot Brown, the landscape gardener, was called
the setter's reading: yes for the gardener, and certainly not for Gordon Brown, a jibe at his competence

explanation.walkthrough: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown was an 18th-century English garden designer; the joke is that the Brown in power at the time showed none of this quality.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden designer Lancelot Brown got his nickname from telling clients their estates had potential for improvement.

clue.text: (+ 11ac.) Reading fan has work out in middle of bang

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
putting something in the middle of a word sets it inside

blocks.note: a boom is a loud bang
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A supporter of Reading football club has a job going off with a bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading' looks like the English town and its football club, but it is the pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookworm is someone devoted to books, a lover of reading.

clue.text: Sexually obliging given cash (income that's not earned)

blocks.note: easy is slang for sexually available
cash is money

explanation.surface: Someone sexually compliant is paid for it, which hardly counts as earning.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy money is cash gained with little effort, so it is unearned gain rather than wages.
